the repository (or repo) contains the source code and history for a software project. In the case of XT, bitcoin core was forked (copied essentially) to a new location, with a different group of people maintaining it. That new repository now has changes that do not exist in bitcoin core. The block size change represents some, but also quite a few other changes made as well. If you start using XT, future changes will come from the few that have access to that repo. (aka by publishing new versions of XT).

There is more to consider than just the blocksize. When using any software, or variants of, you need to remember this is code executing on your computer, and when it comes to the network that software will enforce it's rules, behaviors and changes.

Ask: What is the process for new features, security fixes, network changes etc.. for Bitcoin Core? What is the process for new features, security fixes, network changes etc.. for Bitcoin XT? Will there be the same level of testing? Maintaining a fork has it's own sets of problems in addition. Will all Core features/fixes merge into XT? will some be left out? Will new things in XT be merged to Core? Has anyone actually looked at the new code/commits in XT yet? What happens at the next crossroad/disagreement?

A lot of the development questions have answers in README files and on the webpages. But you should read them when making decisions like this, don't assume anyone else has. Everyone assumes someone else did, and yet not everyone is agreeable to your own ideals anyway.

There's more at stake here than block sizes and names. Just be informed.

consensus originations are vulnerable to halting states like the one we've seen in Bitcoin due to the block size and other network wide issues. Because Bitcoin is provided with an open source license it has been formed numerous times to create alt coins, but this fork is different because it creates two versions of the Bitcoin chain.

Depending on how many miners switch, we could see a fast decisive transition away from Core to XT, or we could have two long term branches of the chain, one running Core, the other XT. In the second scenario the coin base is effectively cloned to the two chains, coins you had before the schism would exist and be spendable on both sides of the fork, effectively doubling the number of coins in circulation and presumably pushing down the exchange value of both.

I think you are mostly right about this. Yes, this is a struggle about how decisions should be made in Bitcoin. No, it's not about whether Bitcoin should be run by the Bitcoin Core developers or the Bitcoin XT developers.

Rather, it's a decision about whether Bitcoin decisions should be made by the Bitcoin Core developers or by the miners. I don't think anyone considers Bitcoin XT to be some privileged Chosen Program. Gavin Andresen is not the One True Heir of MohammedSatoshi. He just made a piece of software that a lot of people think is better for Bitcoin than Bitcoin Core. If someone makes a version that's better than Gavin and Mike's, we'll switch to that.

Bitcoin Core proponents say that there is no Bitcoin but Bitcoin Core, and the Core Developers are its prophet.

Bitcoin XT proponents say that any client that uses the Bitcoin blockchain is valid, and that the chain with the most proof of work represents Bitcoin, regardless of the name of the client that generated it.

One of those two paths is more centralized than the other. Since decentralization is a core tenet of Bitcoin, I would argue that Bitcoin XT is more bitcoiny at its core than Bitcoin Core.

ELI5: Why aren't phones capable of adjusting volume in smaller increments?

Sounds volume increases logarithmically. For every 3db increase in volume, it doubles in strength. So if you make every volume click increase the signal amplification by a couple db, it becomes loud very quickly. The alternative is you set each click to represent half a db and now you're clicking 50 times to move it from silent to "faintly audible".
There are tweaks you can get that change this. No clue on android, but on iOS you can get VolumeAmplifier.
